device.name: LeggedRLLab cross-embodied G1+Go2 flat locomotion (Isaac Lab)

facts.text: The repository targets Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and Isaac Lab 2.3.0 and its documented environment uses Python 3.11
The cross-embodied G1+Go2 flat task is registered as LeggedRLLab-Isaac-CrossEmboided-Flat-G1Go2-Mixed-v0 with CrossEmbodiedG1Go2Env as its entry point
The scene spawns a 29-DOF Unitree G1 and a 12-DOF Unitree Go2 in every environment; the first n // 2 environments make G1 active and the second half make Go2 active
The shipped configuration sets num_envs to 512 with an environment spacing of 4.0 m
The policy action is one unified 29-dimensional vector; G1 uses all 29 dims and Go2 applies only the first 12 and discards dims 12-28
The raw action is scaled by 0.5 for G1 and 0.25 for Go2
The action term computes scaled = action * scale and joint targets = default joint position + scaled, and stores the Go2-masked scaled action in _last_scaled
last_action_cross clones action_manager.action and zeroes unused Go2 dimensions
The policy joint velocity observation has scale 0.05 and last_action uses last_action_cross
The critic joint velocity observation has scale 0.05 and last_action uses last_action_cross

The actor observation is 98 dimensions [robot_id(2), base angular velocity(3), projected gravity(3), command(3), joint position(29), joint velocity(29), last action(29)] and the critic observation is 101 dimensions, adding base linear velocity(3)
The velocity command samples x and y linear velocity and yaw rate uniformly from -1.0 to 1.0 and resamples them every 10 s
Termination selects base_below_threshold_cross with min_height 0.25 and mdp.time_out with time_out=True
The control period is four 5 ms simulation steps (20 ms) and the configured episode length is 20 s
The G1 initial-state configuration sets pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.8)
The shared alive reward term has weight 0.15
is_alive_cross returns the inverse of termination_manager.terminated as floats
The package setup metadata declares license Apache 2.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's command draw and the episode state; the kinematic transition is deterministic, so one seed and action sequence repeats a trajectory on this fake.  The upstream environment draws randomisation from torch and Isaac Lab generators, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two.

gaps: no rigid-body dynamics: joint positions are set directly from the scaled action, with no contacts, friction, gravity, actuator, sensor or noise model (F0 kinematic model, not the Isaac Sim physics)
the fake models one G1 environment, not the configured 512 environments (half G1, half Go2); the Go2 branch, its 12-joint action slice and the 12-28 zero padding are not modelled

the real environment is vectorized: its observations are batched (num_envs, 98) and (num_envs, 101) tensors and reward/terminated/truncated are (num_envs,) tensors, while the fake returns one environment's 98 and 101 values and scalar reward and flags

the fake publishes an unbounded 29-element action Box because the clone's action term (cross_embodied_mdp.py:689-710) defines no clip; the external Isaac Lab action manager's own space was not inspected, so no finite action bound is claimed
the base-height transition is a synthetic kinematic placeholder, so the 0.25 m base-fall termination is exercised by the fake's height rule, not by rigid-body dynamics
the fake uses weight 0.15 as a synthetic per-step alive score, zero on termination; the external reward manager's integration and every tracking, gait, contact and joint penalty term are omitted

the observation values are analytic: projected gravity is constant, base angular and linear velocity are zero and joint velocity is a finite difference of commanded offsets with the configured 0.05 observation scale; last_action reports the raw action, not the action term's scaled target
the fake samples commands with Python's random.Random and does not model the 2 percent standing environments or the command manager's own generator
no rendering, no snapshot and restore (the environment exposes no get_state/set_state) and no GPU or Isaac Sim work
the upstream environment needs Isaac Sim 5.1.0, Isaac Lab 2.3.0 and a GPU (README.md:3-5); it was not installed or run here and the fake was never compared with it

only fake is declared: the implicit gymnasium.make fallback supplies no required cfg (g1go2_flat_env_cfg.py:573-578), AppLauncher lifecycle (scripts/rsl_rl/train.py:59-61), task registration import, tensor action batch or vector reward/flag adapter; it is not a supported live route
the fake ends an episode at its synthetic 1000-step counter and requires an explicit world reset; the inherited Isaac Lab automatic-reset and timeout-counter lifecycle were not reproduced
the source parking helper sets world z to _PARK_ALTITUDE (g1go2_flat_env_cfg.py:607-615), rather than adding that value to the origin z; the fake omits inactive-robot parking entirely
the repository also ships Go1/G1 hardware deployment scripts and Unitree SDK submodules; none is imported or served by this fake-only package
the card retains NOASSERTION and publication review is required despite Apache 2.0 setup metadata and source headers; no root-wide license grant is inferred from those files

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: on the declared fake backend, the lockstep stand-in stops advancing: no step, world reset or seed command is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the cached state stays readable and clearing the latch alone changes no state; this establishes no Isaac Sim stop
